input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 2.1 is the only clause imposing a purchase commitment on us, and it is a multi-year take-or-pay (USD 2,000,000 per year for three years) expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — walk-away territory under MINCOMMIT and well short of the fallback, which would require the commitment to be limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, and true-up rather than penalty based. It also contradicts § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges that "Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment," and sits awkwardly with § 7.1, under which we pay the Fees stated in each Order Form and Vendor may not impose an unidentified minimum-use charge. We therefore replace the take-or-pay sentence with the preferred position (no minimum purchase or volume commitment; payment only for usage or ordered Services), which is the shortest change and removes the § 12.3 conflict; the fallback structure is offered in the comment if Vendor needs some commitment. Other "shortfall" references (§§ 22.2–22.3) concern audited licence underpayments, not a volume commitment, and are not flagged.

proposal.summary: Replace the three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay in § 2.1 with a no-minimum-commitment, pay-for-what-is-ordered provision.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right, so we have replaced Section 2.1 with our preferred position: no minimum purchase or volume commitment, with Customer paying only for usage or Services ordered under an Order Form (consistent with Sections 7.1 and 12.3). If some commitment is essential, we could discuss one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
